candidates.C1: My fitness watch logged four thousand steps while I slept last night, so I laughed it off as a faulty sensor. This morning it congratulated me on my early walk, and the front door was still locked from the inside.
candidates.C2: My dashcam saves a ten-second clip whenever it senses motion, so I check it every morning over coffee. Today's clip showed my car parked in my own driveway, and me walking away from it toward the woods at two in the morning.
candidates.C3: I fill my mother's pill box every Sunday, one compartment for each day, and she has never missed a dose. This Sunday every compartment was empty, and she has been in the ground since March.
candidates.C4: Our dog barks at the back door every night at eleven, and I have learned to ignore him. Tonight he is silent, and the back door is standing open.
candidates.C5: The elevator in my building has been stopping on the thirteenth floor every night, though the button for it was removed years ago. Last night it stopped on my floor, and the doors opened on an empty car with my name scratched into the mirror.
candidates.C6: The delivery driver always leaves my groceries on the porch and rings twice. Tonight there was only one ring, and the bags were already inside, lined up on the kitchen counter.
candidates.C7: My son's teacher called to say he drew our family again in class today. There were five of us in the picture, and the fifth was standing behind me, holding my hand.
candidates.C8: I hang my laundry on the line every morning, and every evening I bring in exactly what I hung out. This evening there was one extra shirt, my size, still warm.
candidates.C9: My phone's voice recorder has been saving a three-second clip at 3:12 a.m. every night this week. I played tonight's clip back, and it was my own voice counting down from ten, in a room where I was sleeping alone.
